content.text: This tool provides an auto-updating generation widget for these jobs. Do not call job_display, show_generations, or show_generation_by_ids to display these jobs again, either before or after completion, unless the user explicitly requests a separate display. If you need to await completion, use jobs_wait with timeout_seconds <= 15. Use job_display only if the user explicitly requests a separate re-display of one specific job.

Note: adjustments applied — medias[0].role: "image" → "image_references" (Nano Banana 2.1 backend expects schema-key media roles); medias[1].role: "image" → "image_references" (Nano Banana 2.1 backend expects schema-key media roles).

Submitted 1 job. If a widget is visible, it polls automatically — do not call job_status or show_generations as a follow-up poll. In text-only clients, use job_status with sync:true to poll for completion.
- 7ec798b1-6c7f-4e21-9db7-b92b0ad13f5d  "Use IMAGE1 as the base. Make exactly one local cartoon-effect edit. Keep IMAGE1's monkey, face, posture, TWO WOODEN STICKS AND THEIR EXACT LENGTHS, forest, lighting, tail, feet and camera unchanged. All wood remains unlit.

Replace IMAGE1's sweeping yellow arcs and the small low dust puff with IMAGE2's compact fluffy cream HAND CLOUD. The new cloud must COVER BOTH VISIBLE FISTS COMPLETELY at the center of the monkey's belly, hiding the fast hands inside. It is centered on the fists, higher than the current low puff. Use the same cloud size and scalloped cream shape as IMAGE2, spanning about x30–56% and y61–70% of the portrait. Two forearms enter it; the exposed stick X and both upper stick ends remain completely visible above the cloud. A few short curved ochre strokes stay INSIDE the cloud, like IMAGE2. No giant sweeping arcs outside it, no cloud below the knees, no added hands, no fire or glow. Copy only IMAGE2's hand-cloud effect; retain IMAGE1's longer stick geometry and everything else."

If the user requests a combined display of multiple generations, including jobs submitted through separate generate_* calls, collect all requested job IDs, wait for the complete set with jobs_wait, then call show_generation_by_ids with jobs: [{"index":0,"job_id":"<first actual job ID>"},{"index":1,"job_id":"<second actual job ID>"}, ...]. job_display accepts only one id: never pass ids to it or loop over it to show a group. Do not create an extra display when the existing generation widgets already satisfy the request.
